checks: All nearby cut planes meet an interior ball around 0. For a proper convex section its relative interior lies in the body interior, since a supporting hyperplane at a relative interior point would have to contain the cut plane. The boundary of its projected section is null, including the endpoint case k=1. The bounded horizontal projection and the fiber-length Lipschitz bound justify the first differentiation and give the directional integrand a·z−β over the tilted projected section.

A neighborhood of the compact zero section boundary retains the nonzero horizontal defining gradient after the small graph perturbation. The defining function for the projected section has gradient G_z−hG_t and parameter derivative G_t(β−a·z). At zero the outward speed is −(β−a·z)N_t/||N_z||. Endpoint integration in finitely many implicit-function charts yields the transport derivative, continuous in (h,b), for each moment integrand. These are horizontal-coordinate integrals and do not carry the tilted-plane area factor.

Writing the horizontal-slice speed as s=−N_t/||N_z||, the h derivative of the z-moment integrates −zzᵀs, its b derivative integrates zs, and the b derivative of the negative area integrates −s. This gives exactly −M₂′/V, +M₁′/V, and −S′/V. The horizontal chart has orthonormal derivative, cap fractions are unchanged by positive rescaling of its normal, and the vanishing first derivative is equivalent to M₁(0)=0 since S(0)>0. Substitution of the speed gives the positive N_t boundary-integral sign.
